root_idea.summary: The root's principal semantic orientation is force exerted to overcome or prevail over something or someone.
root_idea.development: This develops into meanings of domination, delegated authority, and proof understood as something that forcefully establishes a claim. Related lexical branches extend force and sharpness to physical qualities and speech, while the oil sense is treated as a divergent dialectal branch.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested Form II verb has an independently supported causative meaning.
The Quran-attested nominal has distinct authority/power and proof/evidence uses.

senses.definition: To give or assign power, authority, or mastery over someone; to cause someone to prevail over another.
senses.usage_conditions: A causative construction, commonly followed by عَلَى, expressing the granting or exercise of superior power over an object.

senses.definition: Authority, power, or dominion exercised over others or granted to an agent.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for effective or delegated power and authority, including power attributed to or denied to Satan and authority granted to a person. In some passages it can denote ruling power rather than an abstract proof.

senses.definition: A proof, evidence, argument, plea, or manifest sign that establishes or forcefully demonstrates a claim.
senses.usage_conditions: Corresponds to حُجَّةٌ or بُرْهَانٌ and can include a manifest miracle or sign. In passages such as 17:33 and 69:29, the word is explicitly compatible with either authority/power or a plea.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To overcome, prevail, or predominate; to become established in superior power and possess dominion or rule.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive Form I verb describing prevailing power or sovereignty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become strong or hard, especially of a solid hoof or a camel's foot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to physical objects whose hardness or strength is being described.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become sharp; of a person or speech, to be eloquent and sharp-tongued, long-tongued, clamorous, or foul-tongued.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The speech-related applications describe forceful or cutting expression; the source gives both commendatory and blameworthy uses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To overcome, prevail, or exercise superior power, dominion, or authority over others; to receive or be made to have such power.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive or quasi-passive Form V counterpart of سَلَّطَ عَلَيْهِمْ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A ruler, governor, king, sovereign, or caliph; a person vested with ruling power.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A person-denoting application of the noun, distinct from its abstract sense of authority or proof.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Strength, hardness, sharpness, force, or violence as manifested in a thing; by extension, severe winter, inflamed blood, or blazing fire.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader Classical Arabic application to physical or natural intensity rather than political or evidentiary authority.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Strong or hard, especially describing a solid hoof or a beast with a hard foot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective applied to physical strength or hardness, with hoof and foot as the recorded applications.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sharp, including the sharp edges of the foreparts of hoofs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to things possessing a sharp edge or point.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Eloquent and sharp-tongued; also long-tongued, clamorous, or foul-tongued.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person, speech, or tongue; the speech-related use may be praise or blame depending on the expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Olive oil; in a dialectal usage, sesame oil, and more broadly oil pressed from grains or berries.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The geographic attribution of the sesame-oil sense varies among authorities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: More or most overcoming, prevailing, predominating, or superior in power or force.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A comparative or superlative adjective describing superiority in power.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Most eloquent, chaste, or sharp-tongued in speech.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A comparative or superlative application describing superiority in verbal expression.

cautions: سُلْطَان in several Quranic contexts, especially 17:33 and 69:29, permits an authority/power reading as well as a proof or plea reading; the examples preserve that lexical ambiguity.
The oil sense of سَلِيط is a dialectal branch, and the reported identification of the relevant oil varies between olive oil and sesame oil among authorities.
Classical usage reports سُلْطَان as both masculine and feminine; this grammatical variation does not create a separate lexical sense.
